sentences.en: The other thing I would kind of say is, you know, a lot of what people have done in that context is, is, is to do an Evelyn Hooker type project to say, look,
sentences.zh: 我要说的另一件事是，你知道的，人们在这种背景下做的大量工作，就是做一个伊芙琳·胡克（Evelyn Hooker）式的项目，去证明，看，

sentences.zh: 实际上，你知道的，同性伴侣和异性伴侣之间的关系并没有那么大区别。

sentences.en: And I think that's, that's probably right on the left wing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这，这在左翼看来可能是对的。

sentences.en: Lots of people have fantasies that, you know, LGBT people will, you know, dismantle lots of oppressive structures simply

sentences.en: by being, and on the right wing, lots of people have fantasies that LGBT people will like dismantle status quo structures simply by being.
sentences.zh: 而在右翼，许多人也有幻想，认为LGBT群体会像通过存在一样瓦解现状结构。

sentences.en: And, um, we are neither the angels or monsters of these imaginations.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我们既不是这些想象中的天使，也不是怪物。

sentences.en: We are ordinary people who, you know, eat breakfast and walk dogs and drive cars and, you know, worry about carbon footprints and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们是普通人，你知道的，吃早餐、遛狗、开汽车，并且，你知道的，担心碳足迹之类的事情。

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of psychological research just does that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多心理学研究正是在做这件事。

sentences.en: It kind of says, uh, actually things are not so different.
sentences.zh: 它有点像在说，嗯，实际上情况并没有那么不同。

sentences.en: And so it was very, very obvious, I think, to a lot of people who were in any way involved in LGBT
sentences.zh: 因此，对于任何以某种方式参与到LGBT社群中的人来说，这都是非常非常显而易见的，

sentences.en: communities that people had always been living in very long-term relationships where they were
sentences.zh: 人们一直生活在非常长期的关系中，他们

sentences.en: completely, you know, mutually interconnected in loving lifelong ways with people of the same gender forever, forever.
sentences.zh: 完全地，你知道的，以充满爱意和终身相伴的方式与同性伴侣永远、永远地相互交织在一起。

sentences.en: And I think when the state woke up and said, what, what, what, what are we going to call these things to recognize them?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当国家醒悟过来并说：什么，什么，什么，我们该怎么称呼这些关系来承认它们？

sentences.en: Like, it would be hard to think of a better, a better model for that than marriage.
sentences.zh: 就像，很难想出一个比婚姻更好的模式了。

sentences.en: So, so that was all very important.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以这一切都非常重要。

sentences.en: I think there is also always questions about whether that push around marriage and it was quite strong.
sentences.zh: 我认为，关于围绕婚姻的这种推动力——而且它相当强大——也一直存在着疑问。

sentences.en: Um, I remember being at the APA in 2010
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得2010年在APA开会的时候，

sentences.en: and I just remember like, you could have gone to a talk about equal marriage pretty much any hour of the day of the five days of that conference.
sentences.zh: 我只记得，在那次为期五天的会议的每一天里，你几乎随时都能去听一场关于平等婚姻的讲座。

sentences.en: I was like, okay, um, I think I want to go hang out with the historians now.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想：好吧，嗯，我想我现在要去找历史学家们呆在一起了。

sentences.en: This is, this is, I feel like I've been married at a little bit here.
sentences.zh: 这，这，我感觉在这里有点“被结婚”了。

sentences.en: Um, and I think, you know, people had good claims that there were other things that were happening that were
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为，人们有充分的理由认为还有其他事情正在发生，

sentences.en: a much, much more pressing concern to important LGBT communities that were being silenced by the marriage thing.
sentences.zh: 这些事情对重要的LGBT社群来说是更加紧迫的关切，却被婚姻这个话题给压制或消声了。

sentences.en: So yeah, psychological research, very, very important.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，心理学研究非常非常重要。

sentences.en: But I think also the question of how central marriage became in that platform of LGBT rights in general, and particularly within
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，婚姻在整个LGBT权利纲领中变得有多么核心，特别是在APA内部，这也是一个值得思考的问题，即在这个过程中同时还发生了什么，

sentences.en: So if, as you were saying, the, the situation in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，美国的局势

sentences.en: is, is distinct because of our Supreme Court, the way that we're structured and
sentences.zh: 由于我们的最高法院、我们的结构方式而显得与众不同，

sentences.en: the court cases have been really important, but not so much in other countries, is the research still
sentences.zh: 并且法庭案件确实非常重要，但在其他国家并非如此，那么这项研究对于其他同样在努力应对婚姻平等问题的国家来说，

sentences.zh: 仍然有用吗？

sentences.en: Somewhat.
sentences.zh: 有点用。

sentences.en: But I think ultimately what you would want is you would want these rights to be given not on the basis of convincing people by psychological research.
sentences.zh: 但我想最终你的期望是，这些权利的赋予不应该是基于通过心理学研究去说服别人。

sentences.en: Do you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I think that only takes you so far.
sentences.zh: 我认为那只能起到有限的作用。

sentences.en: Um, what's the other argument that, that it's the right thing to do, that it's just, that it's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，另一个论点是什么呢？那就是这样做是正确的，仅仅因为这是正确的事。

sentences.en: That's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是正确的事。

sentences.en: So, um, I mean, two people who are really important in this history, um, are, uh, a lesbian couple here in Britain called Sue Wilkinson and Celia Kitzinger,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我的意思是，在这段历史中有两个非常重要的人物，嗯，是英国的一对女同性恋伴侣，名叫苏·威尔金森（Sue Wilkinson）和西莉亚·基青格（Celia Kitzinger），

sentences.en: um, who did incredibly important work, um, set up the journal Feminism and Psychology, set up the lesbian and gay section of the British Psychological Society, um, really important
sentences.zh: 嗯，她们做了极其重要的工作，创办了《女性主义与心理学》杂志，建立了英国心理学会的女同性恋和男同性恋分会，进行了

sentences.en: qualitative research on, you know, women's health and lesbian identity and a thousand other things.
sentences.zh: 关于女性健康、女同性恋身份以及其他成千上万个课题的极其重要的定性研究。

sentences.en: And they, um, I mean, you can read their story for yourself.
sentences.zh: 而且她们，嗯，我的意思是你可以自己去阅读她们的故事。

sentences.en: It's, if you look at the psychology's feminist voices website, their oral history is there and they talk about this.
sentences.zh: 如果你去看心理学女性主义之声（Psychology's Feminist Voices）网站，她们的口述历史就在那里，她们在上面谈论了这些。

sentences.en: Um, but they took a case to the Supreme court here in the UK with two other couples.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是她们和其他两对伴侣一起，将一个案件带到了英国最高法院。

sentences.en: Um, they had a Canadian marriage at the time and they once recognized in the UK, Sue had been living in Canada for a while
sentences.zh: 嗯，她们当时在加拿大结过婚，并希望在英国获得承认，苏曾在加拿大住过一段时间，

sentences.en: and, um, they lost their case and had to pay their courts.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，她们输掉了官司，不得不支付诉讼费。

sentences.en: You know, they had to pay the expenses of that, uh, which went into the thousands.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她们必须支付这笔费用，高达数千英镑。

sentences.en: Um, and you know, that was like, I think maybe about 2006 or so.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，那大概是，我想大概是2006年左右吧。

sentences.en: And the judgment given at that point in time was, you know, just simply it's tradition that marriage is a man and a woman.
sentences.zh: 当时做出的判决，你知道的，非常简单，就是传统认为婚姻是一个男人和一个女人之间的事。

sentences.en: And now look, you know, where things are.
sentences.zh: 而现在你看，你知道，事情发展到什么地步了。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, so I think there are, you'd want to bring that argument on other grounds.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道的，所以我想如果你想提出这个论点，需要从其他基础入手。

sentences.en: I mean, the other place that's really interesting is Ireland here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，另一个非常有趣的地方是爱尔兰。

sentences.en: I could linger on this story for a while.
sentences.zh: 我可以在这个故事上多停留一会儿。

sentences.en: I wasn't in Ireland the day of this vote.
sentences.zh: 投票那天我不在爱尔兰。

sentences.en: And, um, cause I live overseas, I don't have a vote in Ireland for good reasons.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，因为我住在海外，出于种种原因我在爱尔兰没有投票权。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, the day that this marriage referendum went down, it was kind of like, I got all of these sort of like emails and messages from people I
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是你知道，在这个婚姻公投通过的那天，那种感觉就像是，我收到了所有这些，嗯，来自那些我

sentences.en: hadn't heard from in years, like years.
sentences.zh: 多年未曾联系过的人的电子邮件和信息，真的是多年。

sentences.en: I mean, decades, um, people, I like a guy I shared a flat with in California, like 20 years earlier, I completely lost contact with, which emailed me from Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几十年，嗯，人们，就像一个20年前在加利福尼亚和我合租过公寓的家伙，我们完全失去了联系，他竟然从夏威夷给我发了邮件。

sentences.en: Like you're a very senior researcher in Europe who I greatly admire.
sentences.zh: 就像：你是一位在欧洲备受我景仰的资深研究员。

sentences.en: Like, even like, it was like that when Ireland voted, you know, it's like everybody wants to
sentences.zh: 甚至就像是，在爱尔兰投票表决时就是这种情形，你知道的，每个人都想

sentences.en: touch an Irish gay person, you know, I was the available Irish gay person in some people's network and they wanted to, that was lovely.
sentences.zh: 接触一个爱尔兰同性恋者，你知道的，我就是某些人社交圈里那个随叫随到的爱尔兰同性恋，他们想要这么做，那真的很可爱。

sentences.en: You know, that was so amazing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, I mean, what happened psychologically in Ireland was very interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是你知道的，我的意思是，爱尔兰发生的心理学层面的事情非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I think it was
sentences.zh: 并且我认为它

sentences.en: informed by some of the things that happened in the U S particularly in California.
sentences.zh: 受到了美国、特别是加利福尼亚发生的一些事情的影响。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: and the actress in Ireland had a very sustained campaign of personally touching every person in the country.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰的活动人士开展了一场非常持久的运动，亲自接触了国内的每一个人。

sentences.en: You know, they knocked on doors.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们挨家挨户敲门。

sentences.en: Everybody had a face-to-face conversation.
sentences.zh: 每个人都进行了一对一的对话。

sentences.en: And I think as a result, everybody thought deeply about this issue.
sentences.zh: 我想结果就是，每个人都对这个议题进行了深入的思考。

sentences.en: And that's a very different kind of thinking from putting up some research and saying, ha ha, your side is wrong.
sentences.zh: 这与抛出一些研究然后说：哈，哈，你们这一边是错的，我们这一边是对的，这种思考方式截然不同。

sentences.en: Our side is right.
sentences.zh: 我们这一边是对的。

sentences.en: This group is similar or this group is different, which is a mode of argument you can do with psychological research, which is very common in, in the U S.
sentences.zh: 这个群体是相似的还是这个群体是不同的——这是你可以通过心理学研究进行的一种争论模式，在美国非常普遍。

sentences.en: But I think what they did in Ireland was really different.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们在爱尔兰所做的事情真的很不一样。

sentences.en: They engage people in a different kind of thinking.
sentences.zh: 他们让人们参与到一种不同方式的思考中。

sentences.en: It was longer, it was harder and it made sense to do it that way.
sentences.zh: 这个过程更漫长、更艰难，但用这种方式做是很有意义的。

sentences.en: And, you know, in Ireland that worked.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这在爱尔兰成功了。

sentences.en: And then I think one of the countries in the former Yugoslavia, I think it was Slovenia at the same time, same year had a marriage referendum as well.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为前南斯拉夫的一个国家，好像是斯洛文尼亚，在同一时期、同一年也举行了婚姻公投。

sentences.en: And it went against them again by two thirds majority.
sentences.zh: 结果他们又一次以三分之二的多数票反对了。

sentences.en: And they didn't do that there.
sentences.zh: 而他们在那里并没有这样做。

sentences.en: If I understand it rightly, you know, they didn't get into rural community.
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，你知道的，他们没有深入到农村社区。

sentences.en: They didn't have that kind of penetration.
sentences.zh: 他们没有做到那种程度的渗透。

sentences.en: So I think what is real change?
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为什么是真正的改变？

sentences.en: What is lasting change?
sentences.zh: 什么才是持久的改变？

sentences.en: I think it very often does involve deep conversations rather than here's my research.
sentences.zh: 我认为它往往确实需要深入的对话，而不是拿着我的研究说：现在我证明了你是错的。

sentences.en: Now I've proved you wrong.
sentences.zh: 现在我证明了你是错的。

sentences.en: Like that has a place in argumentation.
sentences.zh: 那种方式在辩论中有一席之地。

sentences.en: It's a place in conversation, but it's not the whole of us.
sentences.zh: 它在对话中有一席之地，但它并非我们的全部。

sentences.en: And I think psychologists who do that kind of research need to recognize it's not the whole of us.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为做这种研究的心理学家需要认识到，这并不是我们的全部。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And certainly we have that history here in the U S I mean, where the courts have occasionally been ahead of where the populace is for example, Brown versus board of education.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在美国确实也有这样的历史，我的意思是，法院有时会领先于民众的立场，例如布朗诉教育委员会案。

sentences.en: You know, we didn't, uh, I mean, we're still fighting that, that, that war, you know, the, the racism in our country is, is quite pervasive and
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们没有，嗯，我的意思是，我们仍在进行那场，那场，那场战斗，你知道的，我们国家的种族主义非常普遍，并且

sentences.en: you can't just change people's hearts and minds because a court says that this is what you need to do.
sentences.zh: 你不能仅仅因为法院说这是你需要做的事，就去改变人们的心智。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's an excellent, an excellent point.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个极好的，极好的观点。

sentences.en: Um, I wanted to, um, talk about your other work, your experimental research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，嗯，谈谈你的另一项工作，你的实验研究。

sentences.en: I know one of your recent papers on auditory gaydar found that people may discriminate against quote unquote, lesbian sounding women and gay sounding men when they're
sentences.zh: 我知道你最近关于听觉“同性恋雷达”（gaydar）的一篇论文发现，人们在做出招聘决策时，可能会对所谓的“听起来像同性恋”的女性和“听起来像同性恋”

sentences.en: making hiring decisions.
sentences.zh: 的男性产生歧视。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你能稍微谈谈那项研究吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以的。

sentences.en: I, I just, uh, massive shout out to Fabio Fasoli, um, who is the real genius in this.
sentences.zh: 我，我只想，嗯，向法比奥·法索利（Fabio Fasoli）致以崇高的敬意，他才是这其中的真正天才。

sentences.en: Um, Fabio is an Italian psychologist who, who works at the university of Surrey, who has published extensively on auditory
sentences.zh: 嗯，法比奥是一位意大利心理学家，在萨里大学工作，他发表了大量关于听觉

sentences.en: gaydar and, and the kinds of discrimination it can bring around.
sentences.zh: “同性恋雷达”以及它可能带来的各种歧视的研究成果。

sentences.en: He, uh, worked as a postdoc fellow with me for two years in Surrey.
sentences.zh: 他，嗯，曾在萨里郡和我一起做过两年的博士后研究员。

sentences.en: And it was in that context that we did that research.
sentences.zh: 我们正是在那个背景下开展了这项研究。

sentences.en: So gaydar is very often studied in psychology and gaydar is when you kind of, you know, make an
sentences.zh: 所以，“同性恋雷达”在心理学中经常被研究，所谓“同性恋雷达”就是指你基本上会，你知道的，对某人的

sentences.en: inference about somebody's sexual orientation, usually the inference that like, Oh, I no longer assume that person is straight, uh, because of something about them.
sentences.zh: 性取向做出推断，通常这种推断就像是：“哦，由于这人的某些特质，我不再默认他是异性恋了，嗯。”

sentences.en: Um, it can be an aspect of their physical appearance or something about the way they move or in our studies, something about the way that they speak.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可能是他们外表的一个方面，或者他们走路姿势的某些特点，在我们研究中，则是他们说话方式的某些特点。

sentences.en: So in these studies, people listened to very, very short extracts of talk, which were said to be from interviews where people were being interviewed for leadership positions in
sentences.zh: 所以在这些研究中，人们聆听了非常非常简短的讲话片段，据说这些片段摘自人们接受访谈的录音，当时他们正面试

sentences.en: various roles.
sentences.zh: 各种职位的领导岗位。

sentences.en: And, uh, they listened to voices that with pretests, we could tell, um, people thought either sounded gay or lesbian or sounded like straight women or men.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，他们听到的声音是我们通过预先测试能够辨别的，嗯，人们认为这些声音听起来像同性恋或女同性恋，或者是听起来像异性恋男女。

sentences.en: And as in other studies, we, we found a discrimination effect so that people who sounded gay or lesbian were, were less likely to be hired for
sentences.zh: 和其他研究一样，我们，我们发现了歧视效应，即那些听起来像同性恋或女同性恋的声音，被录用的可能性

sentences.en: those roles and judged to be less suitable for them as well.
sentences.zh: 更低，并且也被认为不太适合这些角色。

sentences.en: One of the things that was most surprising in those studies, and this, this was a consistent finding across three experiments was that the
sentences.zh: 在这些研究中最令人惊奇的事情之一，而且这在三个实验中是一个一致的发现，那就是

sentences.en: stronger pattern of discrimination was in regard to the women targets.
sentences.zh: 更强烈的歧视模式是针对女性靶标的。

sentences.en: So there was much stronger discrimination against a woman who sounded lesbian compared to a woman who sounded straight than against
sentences.zh: 因此，与听起来像异性恋的女性相比，人们对听起来像女同性恋的女性的歧视要强烈得多，而相比于

sentences.en: a man who sounded gay against, than against a man who sounded straight.
sentences.zh: 听起来像同性恋的男性，对听起来像异性恋的男性则没有那么强烈。

sentences.en: And that's a non-finding because we looked at this the other way.
sentences.zh: 而这是一个意料之外的发现，因为我们从另一个角度来看待这个问题。

sentences.en: So when Fabio has asked, uh, gay and straight women and men, how much do you think your voice communicates your sexual orientation?
sentences.zh: 所以当法比奥询问，嗯，同性恋和异性恋的女性和男性时：“你们认为你们的声音在多大程度上传达了你们的性取向？”

sentences.en: Like men think that much more than women do.
sentences.zh: 比如男性比女性更这样认为。

sentences.en: By the way, when you ask the question, how much do you want your voice to communicate your sexual orientation?
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，当你问这个问题：“你有多希望你的声音传达出你的性取向？”

sentences.en: The group that says they really want that is straight men, right?
sentences.zh: 真正表示他们非常希望这样的群体是异性恋男性，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the group that really wants their voice to communicate sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 那是真正希望自己的声音传达性取向的群体。

sentences.en: We've also like done studies where we've asked lesbian and gay men, like how much do you kind of fear this sort of discrimination, you know, happening to you.
sentences.zh: 我们还做过这样的研究，询问女同性恋和男同性恋，比如你们在多大程度上担心这种歧视，你知道的，会发生在你们身上。

sentences.en: And in that study, you know, gay men more fear it more than lesbians do and so on.
sentences.zh: 在那项研究中，你知道的，男同性恋比女同性恋更担心，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So it's sort of interesting that the, the social representation of gaydar is that it's something that happens to men.
sentences.zh: 所以这就很有趣，关于“同性恋雷达”的社会表征是，它似乎是发生在男性身上的一种现象。

sentences.en: But in this study, it was actually stronger among women.
sentences.zh: 但在本研究中，它实际上在女性中更强烈。

sentences.en: And in most of the discrimination studies, actually, you don't see it just happening to men.
sentences.zh: 而且在大多数歧视研究中，事实上，你不仅会看到它发生在男性身上。

sentences.en: You tend to see it happening to both men and women.
sentences.zh: 你往往会看到它同时发生在男性和女性身上。

sentences.en: So, so yeah, that's, we are working on that.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以是的，我们在研究这个。

sentences.en: We are working on two more papers to figure out that conundrum, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我们正在撰写另外两篇论文来解开这个谜题。

sentences.en: And we have some, some partial answers to it, but let's see if the field thinks they're worthy of publishing.
sentences.zh: 我们对此有一些，一些部分的答案，但让我们看看学术界是否认为它们值得发表。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: I mean, that does sound like a surprising finding to me, largely because, and we get back to the question of sexism and,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来确实是一个令人惊讶的发现，主要是因为，这让我们回到了关于性别歧视的问题，以及，

sentences.en: and sex roles in, in society because being masculine is valued.
sentences.zh: 社会中的性别角色问题，因为阳刚之气是受重视的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And if a woman comes off as being more quote masculine and potentially more gay, then you would think that that would be valued.
sentences.zh: 如果一个女性表现得更具所谓“阳刚之气”且潜在地更像同性恋，那么你可能会认为这会受到重视。

sentences.en: And instead what you're finding is something quite different.
sentences.zh: 然而你发现的却完全不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，不，完全如此。

sentences.en: Thank you for coming back to it.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你重新回到这个话题。

sentences.en: So people have this question, particularly around something like leadership roles in companies, which was the context here.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会有这个疑问，特别是围绕公司里的领导岗位之类的角色，这也是这里的语境。

sentences.en: So that's the context where people supposedly imagine those people as being men by default and value masculine attributes, um, overvalue masculine attributes, one could easily say.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个背景，人们默认会想象那些人是男性，并且看重阳刚的属性，嗯，可以说是过度看重阳刚的属性。

sentences.en: And so you might think that, yeah, stereotyping might go in a lesbian's favor unless, no, we, we, we, we did measure in those studies, how much do you think these
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会认为，是的，刻板印象可能会对女同性恋有利，除非，不，不，不，我们确实在那些研究中测量过，你认为这些

sentences.en: people are masculine or feminine?
sentences.zh: 人有多阳刚或多阴柔？

sentences.en: And you do get some stereotyping effect, but the lesbian is not getting any boost out of that.
sentences.zh: 你确实得到了一些刻板印象的影响，但女同性恋并没有从中获得任何加分。

sentences.en: What's happening is that she is seen as less competent and that seems to be an inference from her perceived sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 实际发生的情况是，她被视为能力较低，而这似乎是从她被感知到的性取向中推断出来的。

sentences.en: That's the more consistent pattern that explains the discrimination across those studies.
sentences.zh: 这是更一致的模式，解释了贯穿这些研究的歧视现象。

sentences.en: So I think a point here, and I think this is, this is kind of difficult for some people maybe to wrap your head around is that, yes, there is this kind of gendery
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这里的一点，而且我认为这，这可能对某些人来说有点难以理解，那就是，是的，确实存在这种关于

sentences.en: kind of stereotyping around gay and lesbian people that happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 同性恋和女同性恋人群的性别化刻板印象，这种现象时刻都在发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's, that's not difficult to capture in experiments, but it's also the case that sexual orientation is still a status variable, right?
sentences.zh: 这，这在实验中并不难捕捉，但同样不可否认的是，性取向仍然是一个地位变量，对吧？

sentences.en: It's still a marker of your status and a marker of your higher status to be straight.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是你地位的一个标志，而作为异性恋则是你拥有更高地位的标志。

sentences.en: And that's why we kind of thought, actually, I think status needs to be thought about in this equation as well.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们觉得，实际上，我认为在这个等式中也需要考虑地位的问题。

sentences.en: When we think about what is the landscape of discrimination that people might encounter, uh, if they are lesbian and gay, or even if they sound lesbian or gay, that's an important
sentences.zh: 当我们思考人们可能会遇到的歧视环境是什么时，嗯，如果他们是女同性恋和男同性恋，或者甚至只是听起来像女同性恋或男同性恋，这是一个重要的

sentences.en: distinction to make, um, and go for leadership positions.
sentences.zh: 需要做出的区分，嗯，并且去竞争领导职位。

sentences.en: And of course, these days, I mean, this podcast is a good example.
sentences.zh: 当然，如今，我的意思是，这个播客就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Like there's some people that you meet only by hearing their voice, you know, and
sentences.zh: 比如有些人你只能通过听到他们的声音来结识，你知道的，而且

sentences.en: you know, since COVID, there's a lot more of this kind of digitally mediated communication as well.
sentences.zh: 自从新冠疫情以来，这种数字媒介的交流也变得多得多了。

sentences.en: Um, so how people sound can, can make a big difference.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以人们听起来怎么样，可能会，会产生很大的影响。

sentences.en: Well, I want to wrap up with a question that takes us back to your book for a moment, because you ended it by writing that it's important
sentences.zh: 好的，我想用一个问题来结束访谈，这个问题把我们带回了你的书，因为你在书尾写道，

sentences.en: for all psychologists to have some knowledge of the recent history of LGBT psychology and that the field
sentences.zh: 所有心理学家都对LGBT心理学的近代史有所了解是很重要的，而且这一领域

sentences.en: offers something of what you call generalizable usefulness beyond gay men and lesbians to whom it initially applied.
sentences.zh: 提供了一些你所谓的具有普遍适用性的价值，超越了它最初适用的男同性恋和女同性恋群体。

sentences.en: Can you, what can psychology, what can the rest of psychology learn from the history of LGBT psychology?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈吗，心理学，心理学的其余部分能从LGBT心理学的历史中学到什么？

sentences.en: I'm glad you picked up on that point.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: And I'm going to,
sentences.zh: 我打算，

sentences.en: I'm going to answer it by sort of thinking about two linguistic terms that are now really common.
sentences.zh: 我打算通过思考两个现在非常普遍的语言学术语来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: So one is coming out.
sentences.zh: 其中一个就是“出柜”（coming out）。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think it'd be really hard to make an argument that coming out as a way of thinking about having a relationship between yourself and shame, it originates anywhere else
sentences.zh: 我想很难有人会反驳这样一种观点：把“出柜”作为一种思考你自身与羞耻感之间关系的方式，它最初并非源于

sentences.en: other than in LGBT culture.
sentences.zh: LGBT文化之外的任何地方。

sentences.en: That would be a little bit tricky to do that particular understanding of it.
sentences.zh: 要对它做出那种特定的理解，其实是有点困难的。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can come out as just about anything now, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，现在你几乎可以对任何事“出柜”，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, so I could come out about the fact that like, I have rejoined our local chess club because I've seen Queen's Gambit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以我可以说出这样一个事实：因为看了《女王的棋局》，我又重新加入了我们当地的国际象棋俱乐部。

sentences.en: It's a little bit shameful, but I, I know my community is there to affirm me.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人羞耻，但我，我知道我的社群会在那里给予我肯定。

sentences.en: You know, I could come out about the fact that I have a taste in particularly distasteful, you know, prog rock, British dad stuff
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可以对这样一个事实“出柜”：我的品味特别低俗，你知道的，是那种20世纪70年代初的

sentences.en: from the early 1970s that's unlistenable for most people.
sentences.zh: 前卫摇滚、英国老爹风，对大多数人来说简直难以下咽。

sentences.en: You know, I can listen to things like, you know, Henry Cow and King Crimson for a long time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可以长时间聆听诸如，你知道的，亨利·考尔（Henry Cow）和国王乐队（King Crimson）的音乐。

sentences.en: That's a little bit shameful.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人羞耻。

sentences.en: It's utterly uncool music, right?
sentences.zh: 这绝对是不酷的音乐，对吧？

sentences.en: But I just, I'm going to venture that on this podcast and, and I hope I live to tell the tale.
sentences.zh: 但我偏要，我打算在这个播客上冒险说出来，而且，我希望我能活着讲完这个故事。

sentences.en: So you can come out about just about anything and that, but that way of thinking,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以对几乎任何事情出柜，而且那种方式，

sentences.en: that way of thinking about the relationship between society and the psyche, uh, disclosure and secrecy,
sentences.zh: 那种思考社会与心灵关系、嗯，披露与秘密的方式，

sentences.en: it would be hard to argue that that is not coming from LGBT culture and its origin.
sentences.zh: 很难反驳说它不是源自LGBT文化及其起源。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of those gifts, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是那些馈赠之一，对吧？

sentences.en: The other one I think is the suffix, a phobia, right?
sentences.zh: 另一个我认为是后缀“-phobia”（恐惧症），对吧？

sentences.en: To describe an irrational kind of prejudice and homophobia, I think originates probably back where you started around the time of the Stonewall uprising in New York.
sentences.zh: 用来描述一种非理性的偏见，而恐同症（homophobia），我认为大概可以追溯到你们开始的地方，也就是纽约石墙起义的时期。

sentences.en: Um, you know, certainly where George
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，当然乔治·温伯格

sentences.en: Weinberg picks it up in his 1973 book and so on.
sentences.zh: 在他的1973年出版的书籍中采用了它，诸如此类。

sentences.en: These days you can use that to describe anything, you know, you can describe fat phobia, you can describe transphobia, you can describe an autism phobia.
sentences.zh: 如今你可以用它来描述任何事物，你知道的，你可以描述恐肥症（fat phobia），你可以描述恐跨症（transphobia），你可以描述恐自闭症（autism phobia）。

sentences.en: Some of my, uh, friends in the intersex world want to talk about intersex phobia, you know, um, and you can apply it to anything.
sentences.zh: 我在双性人世界的一些朋友想谈论恐双性人症（intersex phobia），你知道的，嗯，你可以把它应用到任何事情上。

sentences.en: So, you know, I've even heard Vladimir Putin, you know, talk about Russia phobia, you know, and when I do that, I think that's lovely.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我甚至听过弗拉基米尔·普京，你知道的，谈论恐俄症（Russia phobia），你知道的，当我听到这个时，我觉得这很有意思。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin owes an intellectual debt to LGBT movements.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京对LGBT运动负有知识上的债。

sentences.en: Isn't that all quite lovely?
sentences.zh: 这一切难道不是很美妙吗？

sentences.en: You know, Trump probably talked about some kinds of American phobia as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，特朗普可能也谈到过某种恐美症（American phobia）。

sentences.en: Again, lovely, you know, thank you for acknowledging that intellectual debt, Donald.
sentences.zh: 同样，很美妙，你知道的，感谢你承认这份知识债务，唐纳德。

sentences.en: And, you know, so when you hear these things, I think this is another kind of linguistic or conceptual gift for thinking about things that
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当你听到这些事情时，我认为这是另一种语言或概念上的馈赠，用来思考以下事实：

sentences.en: the prejudice against us just might be completely irrational.
sentences.zh: 对我们的偏见可能完全是不理性的。

sentences.en: Um, because I say we're neither monsters or angels, but we're sort of, you know, ordinary people who eat breakfast and walk dogs and play chess and listen to bad music.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我说过，我们既不是怪物也不是天使，我们某种程度上是，你知道的，吃早餐、遛狗、下国际象棋、听糟糕音乐的普通人。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for joining us today, Dr. Hegarty.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你今天加入我们，黑加蒂博士。

sentences.en: It's been a real pleasure talking to you and really interesting.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈非常愉快，而且真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I hope that we've, uh, taught our listeners a few things about the history of LGBT psychology that they didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们，嗯，已经向听众传授了一些他们以前不知道的关于LGBT心理学历史的知识。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's been a joy.
sentences.zh: 这真是一段快乐的时光。
